key_insight: An ML-guided gut microbiome analysis in STEMI identified a small set of bacterial taxa and predicted metabolic pathways associated with primary VT/VF risk.
clinical_relevance: If validated, these microbiome markers could help improve early risk stratification for dangerous arrhythmias in STEMI patients.
method: Stool samples from 33 STEMI patients were sequenced during acute and recovery phases.
A machine-learning pipeline selected reproducible taxa linked to primary VT/VF.
Functional pathways were inferred with PICRUSt2 from the sequencing data.
evidence_signal: A reduced-feature support vector machine achieved an AUROC of 0.846 (95% CI 0.676-0.984), with 85.7% sensitivity and 76.9% specificity.
watch_item: The cohort was very small and exploratory, so the biomarker signals need validation in larger independent populations before any clinical use.
paper_title: Machine Learning Approach to Identify Gut Microbiota Biomarkers in Patients with ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction Presenting Primary Ventricular Tachyarrhythmias
